notes.title: Free Survival update
notes.content:
[h1]Survival Mode:[/h1]
[list]
	[*]Several characters to choose from with varying speed and toughness
	[*]Rank system - unlockable perks, weapons
	[*]New leaderboards
	[*]Added custom maps for this mode only
	[*]Special weapons
[/list]

[h1]Cheats in Advanced Gameplay Options[/h1]
[list]
	[*]Infinite ammo
	[*]God mode
	[*]Any weapon (including new ones)
[/list]	
   To unlock cheats you must first finish the entire game at least on 'Extreme' difficulty
   
   Cheats are allowed both in Survival mode and in campaign. Using cheats blocks all leaderboards from progressing and almost all achievements (the playtime one keeps ticking only)

   More explaining: If you start a level with cheats enabled (doable from the main menu) you will not get any progress saved for the whole play. You need to exit the level, disable cheats and start with them disabled. Using 'spawn any weapon' cheat blocks saving progress for the map where the cheat was used. If you progress through campaign to next level, the progress from the next level will be saved, although you will have default weapons for that level instead of the ones you had. 
   
   
   
[h1]Two new difficulty settings[/h1]
	[list]Story Mode:
		[*]One additional respawn received at the level start
		[*]You receive 2 respawns per side quest instead of one
		[*]Player has twice the health than on 'Easy' difficulty
		[*]Body Armor is 50% stronger
		[*]A single execution healths to full
		[*]Full health on respawn
	[/list]
	[list]Insane:
		[*] No respawns
		[*] Half the health than on 'Extreme' difficulty
		[*] The game will no longer outline all enemies with a red border when viewing active quests
		[*] Radar does not show people and cars
		[*] Body Armor is 50% weaker
		[*] Rest of the rules ( e.g. health regeneration on execution ) - stays the same relative to the reduced health - you regenerate 20% health each execution just as on 'Extreme' but 20% of lowered health is much less
	[/list]
		
[h1]Hardware Cursor added in the Gameplay Options to reduce noticeable lag when frame rates are low[/h1]
	[list]
	[*] When you enable it, you will be unable to change crosshair color or scale - these options only work with software cursor
	[*] You will not see reload progress around the crosshair
	[*] In exchange you are able to create your custom cursors and use them in our game. Simply put properly prepared *.cur file in the Saved\Cursors catalogue
	[*] If you wish to create animated cursors, you can! They should be placed in the same directory as the regular ones. The supported file extension is *.ani
	[*] To change the hardware cursor icon change the 'Crosshair Type' option. Instead of showing our standard icons it will contain numbers. The number relates to the order in which the files are placed in the folder
	[/list]
	
[h1]New achievements:[/h1]
	[list]
	[*]For completing the game on 'Story Mode' - this one will also unlock after beating the game on any other difficulty. To acquire it you have to finish any level on any difficulty if you have already finished the game
	[*]For completing the game on 'Insane'
	[*]For finishing each level on 'Insane' difficulty with all sidequests
	[*]Survival achievements
	[/list]
	
[h1]Additional side quests for some levels - more respawns for those who need them[/h1]
	[list]
	[*]Two for Army Base
	[*]One for Marina
	[*]One for Downtown
	[/list]
	
[list]
 [*]Added the ability to play 'Truck Stop' or 'Marina' level without having to play through 'Train' or 'Sewers' respectively
 [*]Added option to change sprint behaviour - when on, sprinting no longer requires continuous holding of the 'Run' button. To stop the character from sprinting in this mode you simply press the sprint button again or make an action that prohibits sprinting
 [*]Both civilian and human shields health has been randomized so you will no longer '2shot everyone with pistol'
 [*]Released Steam Cards, Emoticons & Badges
 [*]Borderless windowed mode available in the Graphics Options
 [*]Further performance and stability improvements
 [*]Improved car behaviour - driving
 [*]Multiple bugfixes
 [/list]
 
 
[h1]Known bugs:[/h1]
	[list]
	[*]Some of the UI texts are cut at the end
	[/list]
	
Information:
Players that tested this patch prior to release suggested we allow more bodies to be lying on the map. Default is 50 and we decided to not increase it due to performance reasons. However, we've also decided to not ignore the request, therefore you can modify that value through config file, located at "Hatred\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor\Game.ini". Simply paste at the end of the file:
 
[/Script/Hatred.HatredSurvivalGameMode]
MaximumNumberOfRagdolls=50

You can choose how many corpses should be left alone. Keep in mind that it has an impact on performance, so make sure your PC can handle it. Survival maps are much smaller than the campaign ones, they run faster.

notes.title: Patch nr. 5
notes.content:
- fixed some reported crashes
 - improved performance on AMD processors during heartbeat/flashbang effects
 - reduced range for soldiers in order to prevent them from shooting outside of the screen
 


 Since we're adding tons of new options in this patch, we've decided to explain what these are. I've allowed myself to quote UE4 documentation on some of those.
 
[h1] Gameplay tab: [/h1]
 
	[b]Crosshair scale[/b] - added 3rd option that modifies the crosshair so you have more ways to play with it to make it more visible. Changing the icon, color and scale will most certainly help you fit it to your needs.
 
 [h1]Advanced Graphics tab:[/h1]
 
	[b]Detail Mode[/b] - On lower settings cuts out certain objects and effects that are more expensive.
	
	[b]Lens Flares[/b] - Controls the quality. When set to LOW the effect is not used and turned off. "The Lens Flare effect is an image-based technique that simulates the scattering of light when viewing bright objects due to imperfections in camera lenses."
 
	[b]Decals[/b] - On lower settings decals exist in the world shorter. Decals are mainly blood effects on floors and walls, gunshot holes and explosions on ground.
 
	[b]Destruction system[/b] - On LOW you can destroy only few physics meshes that affect the gameplay. On high it uses all the physics we allow. Helps mainly when you destroy half the city and it starts going slower and slower.
 
	[b]Frame rate cap[/b] - we've received many requests about several features, this is one of them. Caps the frame rate to the value specified. Keep in mind that if you have VSync enabled and your refresh rate is lower than the cap requested, VSync will dominate the setting.
 
	[b]Screen percentage[/b] - a technique that can be used both to improve performance or increase the visual quality. Default is 100. The number specifies at what % should the scene be actually rendered within the engine. Afterwards it is scaled to the actual resolution that you set. Choosing 50% with resolution 1920x1080 means that the scene will be rendered at 960x540 and then upscaled. Will look worse, might work better for your configuration, worth checking. If set to 200 in my example, it means that the actual render resolution will be 3840x2160 and then scaled down resulting in much better looks. 400 (maximum) requires very very high end GPU to run at any decent frame. We've decided to add it as a possible optimization, but since the very same variable can improve quality, you can play with it as well. Will work great for very high quality screens ;)
 
	[b]V-Sync[/b] - there were issues with this settings, we've fixed those we could find, let us know if it still causes problems. If so, attach dxdiag so we can dig deeper.
 
	[b]Ambient Occlusion[/b] - "effect that approximates the attenuation of light due to occlusion." We're noticed that this is one of the effects that causes massive ATI cards performance drops, so here it is for you to try.
 
	[b]Global Illumination[/b] - real-time, dynamic indirect lighting technique. This simulates the sun light actually bouncing off surfaces and coming through the opened doors, through windows and so on. In some places the change when disabling this effect will be barely noticeable (outdoors), but huge part of our scene lighting depends on that effect (since you can destroy all the map, the light has to update accordingly). We're allowing you to disable it to improve performance. It is heavy on all configurations, but to a higher degree on ATI/AMD setups.
 
	[b]Film grain[/b] - allows you to disable the movie film grain effect on the camera. You requested it, so here you got it.
 
	[b]Chromatic aberration[/b] - "effect that simulates the color shifts in real-world camera lenses. The effect is mostly noticeable near the edges of the image." There were several requests to get rid of it, so now you can simply turn it off.
 

 We do realize that solution 'turn off option X if using ATI card' is far from ideal to say the least, but that is what we can do in such a short amount of time. You may switch 1 option off and get FPS boost big enough to play it with no issues. Your choice. We'll keep digging, but can't make any promises whether we find something or not.
 
 If you find some new issues related to these settings do not hesitate to write about it here or contact us. We'll read ;)




Note:
- new settings aren't translated, We will update them in the future.



DC Team

Will look worse, might work better for your configuration, worth checking. If set to 200 in my example, it means that the actual render resolution will be 3840x2160 and then scaled down resulting in much better looks. 400 (maximum) requires very very high end GPU to run at any decent frame. We've decided to add it as a possible optimization, but since the very same variable can improve quality, you can play with it as well. Will work great for very high quality screens ;)

tags.bug: - there were issues with this settings, we've fixed those we could find, let us know if it still causes problems. If so, attach dxdiag so we can dig deeper.

tags.feature: - "effect that approximates the attenuation of light due to occlusion." We're noticed that this is one of the effects that causes massive ATI cards performance drops, so here it is for you to try.

- real-time, dynamic indirect lighting technique. This simulates the sun light actually bouncing off surfaces and coming through the opened doors, through windows and so on. In some places the change when disabling this effect will be barely noticeable (outdoors), but huge part of our scene lighting depends on that effect (since you can destroy all the map, the light has to update accordingly). We're allowing you to disable it to improve performance. It is heavy on all configurations, but to a higher degree on ATI/AMD setups.
- allows you to disable the movie film grain effect on the camera. You requested it, so here you got it.

- "effect that simulates the color shifts in real-world camera lenses. The effect is mostly noticeable near the edges of the image." There were several requests to get rid of it, so now you can simply turn it off.

tags.balance_change: - You may switch 1 option off and get FPS boost big enough to play it with no issues.
